newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom to ease share trade rules.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom to ease share trade rules.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom intends to ease restrictions on trading its shares, the Federal Securities Corporation (FFK) said on Wednesday.
The FFK, which organises regular auctions of Gazprom shares, said trading in the shares would be conducted electronically from late November, and Gazprom would not have first right of refusal.

"By means of this Gazprom has confirmed the seriousness of its intent to gradually move away from its right of first refusal on its own shares, a right which is enshrined in its charter," the FFK said in a statement.
The move could inject more liquidity and transparency into Gazprom shares, which are some of Russia's most illiquid.
The FFK, which conducts auctions of state and other shares for the State Property Fund, said it had reached an agreement with Gazprom and its subsidiary Gazprombank for electronic trading.
The bank would clear the trades.
Only shares acquired through previous FFK auctions will be traded electronically.
The auctions present very small amounts of Gazprom's 23.6 billion shares, each nominally worth 10 roubles.
Gazprom said in August that shareholders wishing to sell could do so only within 90 days after Gazprom, which has first right of refusal, declined to buy them.
The company's charter says that no Gazprom shares can change hands without company approval.

Gazprom last month placed just over one percent of its American Depositary Share (ADS) offering, Russia's largest overseas share issue, raising $429.3 million at $15.75 per ADS, each of which is worth 10 underlying shares.

Gazprom closed at $0.410 on the Russian Trading System on Wednesday, down from $0.434 on Tuesday. At an auction on Tuesday organised by the FKK its shares sold for an average 2,182.32 roubles ($0.400). The ADS was $17.875, up from Tuesday's $17.800 close.
